newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE 35 AND 42 DAY T-BILLS FALL TO 13 PCT.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE 35 AND 42 DAY T-BILLS FALL TO 13 PCT.

text.p: The average yield on the Philippine 35-day and 42-day treasury bills both fell to 13 percent at the auction on Tuesday, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The 42-day bill fell from 17.679 percent and the 35-day bill fell from 17.527.
The highest and lowest bids for both the maturities were also at 13 percent.
It was not known how many bidders had put in tenders.
The Treasury received tenders worth 5.23 billion pesos for the 35-day bills and bids worth 4.245 billion for the 42-day bills. It accepted 500 million pesos for each maturity.
"The rates are much better than we expected. It shows that the rates have normalised," National Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa told Reuters.
She said the Treasury was expecting declines of 415 basis points and more than 420 basis points for the 35-day and 42-day bills respectively.
